definition: Further training an already-pretrained reasoning model with reinforcement learning (typically against a verifiable reward, such as answer correctness) to change its reasoning behavior. In the archive it appears both as a general training stage whose data selection can be made more efficient by predicting which prompts are informative (Dynamics-Predictive Sampling), and as a cause worth scrutinizing: 'Reasoning or Retrieval?' studies how it shifts a model's answers between chain-of-thought reasoning and a memory-retrieval shortcut.

evidence.note: Selects which training prompts to use for RL finetuning of large reasoning models by predicting their learning dynamics with a hidden Markov model, instead of evaluating every candidate with rollouts.
evidence.title: Dynamics-Predictive Sampling for Active RL Finetuning of Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Shows that large reasoning models' final answers are produced by two competing mechanisms, chain-of-thought reasoning and memory retrieval, and introduces FARL, a fine-tuning method that suppresses the retrieval shortcut to encourage genuine reasoning.
evidence.title: Reasoning or Retrieval? A Study of Answer Attribution on Large Reasoning Models

name: reinforcement learning fine-tuning
